newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russia sunseed output to fall 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russia sunseed output to fall 25 percent.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
RUSSIA'S 1996 SUNFLOWER SEED HARVEST FORECAST REVISED DOWN SHARPLY TO 3.1 MILLION TONNES
MOSCOW, Oct 18 - SovEcon has revised downward its forecast for Russia's total sunseed output this year to about 3.1 million tonnes from an earlier forecast of 3.8-4.0 million tonnes.
The new forecast is a full one million tonnes below last year's record production.
Due to a substantial overall decline in output, particularly in the Northern Caucasus, which is the major surplus region, Russia's sunseed exports are likely to fall in 1996/97.
Russia began harvesting its sunseed crop later than usual.
By mid-October, the harvested area amounted to only 1.6 million hectares (only 50 percent of total plantings), compared to 2.4 million ha at the same time last year.
In the Rostov region and Western Siberia, the harvest is particularly behind schedule.
By October 14, Rostov farmers had threshed merely one fifth of the area sown to sunseeds. The harvest in Western Siberia has just started.
The delayed harvest is coupled with reduced yields elsewhere in Russia, except for in the Urals.
As of October 14, the average yield achieved from the harvested area was 0.9 tonnes per ha, or 16 percent below last year's level (Table 1).
The average yield is expected to decline even further, to 0.8 tonnes per ha, as the harvest progresses.
This will be Russia's lowest yield this decade and a full 20 percent below 1995 yields.
The sharpest decline in output is expected in the Northern Caucasus, particularly in the Rostov region, and in Western Siberia.
Output is forecast to increase only in the Urals (Table 2).
